posts.title: chocolate pecan pie bars
posts.description: “Twenty years of Thanksgivings on Smitten Kitchen!” I told Ed Levine yesterday, as we chatted for an upcoming podcast episode [I’ll link it here as soon as it’s live], a statistic that remains baffling to me. What should one even have to show for two decades of Thanksgiving recipes, ideas, and advice? A degree in dry brining? A medal in single-oven-side-dish-rewarming Jenga? A metamorphosis into my final form: a human-shaped holiday cooking questions hotline (it’s me, or at least the texts on my phone)? Aspirationally, all of the above? Read more »

posts.title: skillet pierogi with mushrooms
posts.description: Even though we’re having a relatively warm (and delightful) fall, my cravings for carbs-wrapped-in-carbs, caramelized onions, and earthy skillets of vegetables don’t care. Plus, as we’re in the thick of busy times — this year it’s college applications, middle school adjustments, me, working on a new cookbook for you — any time a full meal can be made in one pan and not feel joyless or compromised, it’s going immediately in our dinner rotation. This sure did. Read more »

posts.title: simple chicken tacos
posts.description: Twenty years ago, I started this website because I wanted a place to share recipes I was excited about, as it’s practically coded into my DNA to be an unfettered yap about the things I love. [ This is me. ] The larger context was that upon reaching so-called adulthood, I’d found that while I knew how to cook, there were still so many things I hadn’t figured out, such as: how to turn a can of tomatoes into not just an okay pasta sauce, but a spectacular one ; how to make really good meatballs ; perfect hummus ; and a crumb cake I’d want to make forever. Read more »
